clue.text: Making some effort to be firm and natural

parts.note: a firm is a company, abbreviated Co
natural, as in inborn, means native

explanation.surface: Someone is trying to be both resolute and unaffected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is just a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Conation is the mental faculty of striving or will, so a conative act is one involving effort.

clue.text: Command an assault

explanation.surface: An order to attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is an order given, and also a headlong attack on an enemy.

clue.text: Base organised in new York — a victory for parliament!

indicators.note: in means the reorganised letters sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: Y is a short form of York

indicators.note: organised means arranged afresh, so the letters of base are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military base set up in New York counts as a parliamentary win.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1645 Battle of Naseby in Northamptonshire was a decisive Parliamentarian victory in the English Civil War; 'organised' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Naseby is the English Civil War battle where Cromwell's New Model Army routed the Royalists.

clue.text: A number, or the singer

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Choosing between a figure and the vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a choice, but TEN plus the plain word OR gives the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

clue.text: Seeing struggle, take flight

parts.note: to struggle against a rival is to vie
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Watching a fight and then running away.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewing something means looking at or watching it.

clue.text: Featherbrains do — it is appalling

indicators.note: appalling means dreadful, so the letters of do, it and is are shaken into a dreadful new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that whatever fools do is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges DO IT IS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Featherbrains are silly, empty-headed people, which is what fools are.

clue.text: Talk the underworld way

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
a course is a route or way

explanation.surface: How people speak in the criminal underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link; 'underworld' means the classical realm of the dead, not gangland.
explanation.definitionFit: A discourse is a lecture, conversation or written treatment of a subject.

clue.text: New-found relation from the other side of the world

definitions.text: from the other side of the world

indicators.note: new-found means freshly made up, so the letters of relation are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recently discovered relative from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New-found' rearranges RELATION into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means of the East, which from Britain lies far across the globe.

clue.text: Burning cigarette-end — giving voice about it!

indicators.note: about means the voice word surrounds the last letter of cigarette

parts.note: giving voice to a tune is singing

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of cigarette

explanation.surface: A smoker's stub is glowing while someone sings about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cigarette-end' looks like a stub, but 'end' just picks the final letter; 'about' means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Singeing is scorching lightly, a form of burning.

clue.text: He wouldn't appear personally, but sent in a worker

indicators.note: in means the word sent is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: a worker bee, so worker can mean bee

explanation.surface: Someone who wouldn't show up in person sent a labourer instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' is a crossword staple for a bee; 'but' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone who stays away rather than turning up in person.

clue.text: Grant a device is without point

indicators.note: is without means the pieces a and device stand outside, around the point

parts.note: a device, like an emblem on a shield, is a sign
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A gadget turns out to have no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: A SIGN goes around S, giving A-S-SIGN. 'point' wants to mean purpose; it is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant something to someone is to allot or hand it over to them.

clue.text: Simple, in father brown's opinion

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words father brown's

explanation.surface: Chesterton's priest-detective Father Brown would think it plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simple' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: an old word for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is a medicinal plant used on its own, which is a herb.

clue.text: Material being read the wrong way

indicators.note: reading something the wrong way garbles it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fabric being misread, perhaps a label misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' rearranges BEING READ into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaberdine is a hard-wearing twill fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: The weight of a big cat!

explanation.surface: A question of how heavy a large feline is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two meanings; the surface pretends to weigh a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a small imperial unit of weight and the snow leopard of Central Asia.

clue.text: A beast will back the use of guns

indicators.note: back means the word for guns is read from its end to its start

parts.note: gats are guns in old American slang, here loosely phrased as the use of guns

explanation.surface: An animal supposedly supports shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' is a link; 'back' looks like support but turns GATS around.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, an animal.

clue.text: Things set to change, allowing of no relaxation

indicators.note: to change means the letters of things set are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Things are about to change, with no easing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges THINGS SET into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightness is the state of being taut, with no slack left.

clue.text: Haggle a good deal

explanation.surface: Haggling to get value for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to negotiate over terms, and a cheap purchase is also called this.

clue.text: Yielded, and bore the expense

explanation.surface: Someone gave in and paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Afforded means provided or gave, and also had the money to pay for something.

clue.text: He'll get to grips with the opposition!

definitions.text: He'll get to grips with the opposition!

parts.words: He'll get to grips with the opposition!
parts.note: reads like a determined politician, but describes a sportsman who literally grapples an opponent

explanation.surface: A determined politician tackling the other party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get to grips' is meant literally: grabbing an opponent's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler grapples bodily with an opponent in a bout.

clue.text: Searches over a lengthy period

explanation.surface: Someone looks around for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FOR AGES, the answer means for a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to rummage about looking for food or supplies; split, it is the phrase meaning for a long time.

clue.text: The boot provides useful stowage

explanation.surface: A car's boot is handy for storing things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boot' is dismissal from a job, not part of a car; 'provides' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fired is getting the sack, and a large bag is handy for storing goods.

clue.text: Those having craft under control talked big

explanation.surface: Sailors in charge of a boat are boasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill but means a vessel; the second meaning is an old past tense of crow, to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company handles the vessel, and an old past tense of crow, to boast, is this word.

clue.text: A mass or just a short prayer!

explanation.surface: A Catholic service, or just a brief prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A mass' as one word, amass, a verb; 'just' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather, and a collect is a short prayer read in church services.

clue.text: American Indian medicine man associated with a bird

parts.note: MO is medical officer, a doctor
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A tribal healer linked with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medicine man' looks like a tribal shaman, matching the surface, but gives MO; 'associated with a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohawk are a Native American people of the Iroquois confederacy.

clue.text: Wait for a series of races to terminate

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the series of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
to terminate is to end

explanation.surface: Waiting for a racing season to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend on someone is to wait upon or serve them.

clue.text: Attack made on cake

parts.note: to cake is to harden into a solid mass, that is to set

explanation.surface: An assault is launched on a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' is a link; 'cake' is a verb, to harden.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is an assault or charge against an enemy.

clue.text: Young runner makes a bloomer

parts.note: a young horse is a colt, and the foot of one gives the name of a yellow wild flower

explanation.surface: A young athlete makes an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Coltsfoot is a yellow-flowered plant, named for its hoof-shaped leaves, so it blooms.

clue.text: Animosity keeps coppers in place!

indicators.note: in means the coins are put inside the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place
coppers are pennies, abbreviated p

explanation.surface: Hostility that keeps police officers where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' is a link; 'coppers' looks like police but means pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite is malice or ill will toward someone.

clue.text: Fifty people are after the same stone table!

indicators.note: after means the pieces fifty and people come behind the piece for the same

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
people means men

explanation.surface: Fifty people are chasing the same stone table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link; DO is the standard shortening of ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolmen is a prehistoric tomb of upright stones topped by a flat slab, like a table.

clue.text: Think to correct imperfections in a friend

indicators.note: in means the correcting word sits inside the word for a friend

parts.note: a mate is a friend
to correct imperfections in a text is to edit it

explanation.surface: Reflect on how to fix a friend's flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'correct imperfections' is one verb phrase, not an adjective plus noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate is to reflect or ponder deeply.

clue.text: Stride off looking most grim

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of stride are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone walks away with a very sullen face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges STRIDE; 'looking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or grim, so the superlative is the grimmest.

clue.text: Moved with all speed when not suited

explanation.surface: Someone raced along without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suited' means clothed; streaking is running naked in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To streak is to dash very fast, and also to run naked through a public place.
